usdRate.sourceName: Swiss National Bank, monthly average foreign exchange rates (devkum), USD 1, October 2026
usdRate.note: Liechtenstein uses the Swiss franc under its currency treaty with Switzerland. October 2026 monthly average CHF 0.82854 per US dollar (SNB devkum, published 2 Nov 2026); September 2026 average 0.8193; World Bank 2025 average 0.831.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Swiss Federal Statistical Office, Swiss consumer price index (LIK) September 2026, adopted monthly by the Liechtenstein Office of Statistics
inflation_cpi.note: Annual CPI inflation +1.0% in September 2026 (0.8% in August). Liechtenstein has no CPI of its own: its Office of Statistics takes over the Swiss national consumer price index each month.

inflation_projection.sourceName: SNB price stability range 0-2% and conditional forecast 0.7% (2026), 0.8% (2027-2028); Swiss CPI averaged about 1.4% a year in 2021-2025
inflation_projection.note: The SNB has kept Swiss-franc inflation inside its 0-2% range almost every year, so 1% is used for long-run planning.

policy_rate.sourceName: Swiss National Bank, monetary policy assessment of 24 September 2026
policy_rate.note: Liechtenstein has no central bank; the Swiss National Bank sets the policy rate for the Swiss franc, unchanged at 0% in September 2026.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: Swiss National Bank, interest rates on new business (zikrepro): savings deposits of private clients, mean
savings_account_rate.note: Mean savings deposit rate 0.069% in September 2026 (same in August) at banks in Switzerland; no separate statistic exists for Liechtenstein banks, which work in the same Swiss-franc market.

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: Swiss National Bank, interest rates on new business (zikrepro): term deposits of CHF 100,000 or more, 3 months, mean
fdr_3m_rate.note: Mean 0.029% in September 2026 (0.026% in August) at banks in Switzerland (Swiss-franc market; no Liechtenstein-only statistic). Covers deposits from CHF 100,000.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: Swiss National Bank, interest rates on new business (zikrepro): term deposits of CHF 100,000 or more, 12 months, mean
fdr_1y_rate.note: Mean 0.152% in September 2026 (0.117% in August) at banks in Switzerland (Swiss-franc market; no Liechtenstein-only statistic); 2-year cash bonds (Kassenobligationen) averaged 0.49%.

dps_rate.note: No monthly recurring deposit product with a published or average rate was found for Liechtenstein; regular saving is done through ordinary savings accounts or fund savings plans.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: No weighted average deposit rate for Liechtenstein banks is published (World Bank FR.INR.DPST has no Liechtenstein figure; FMA statistics give volumes, not rates).

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No government savings certificate or retail savings bond issued by the State of Liechtenstein was found; residents can buy Swiss Confederation bonds in Swiss francs.

tbill_91d_rate.note: The State of Liechtenstein issues no treasury bills. For reference, 3-month Swiss Confederation money-market debt register claims yielded -0.111% in October 2026 (SNB zimoma).

tbond_5y_rate.note: No Liechtenstein government bonds were found; Swiss Confederation bonds are the Swiss-franc benchmark.

tbond_10y_rate.note: No Liechtenstein government bonds were found. For reference, the 10-year Swiss Confederation bond yielded 0.47% on 30 October 2026 (Trading Economics).

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: Liechtenstein Tax Act (Steuergesetz, SteG) Art. 15(1)(a) and Art. 56, consolidated version of 1 July 2026
tax_bank_interest.note: Actual interest is not taxed as income: income from wealth that bears wealth tax is exempt from the income (Erwerb) tax. Instead 4% of net taxable wealth (the Sollertrag, a deemed return) is added to taxable income each year, so savers pay tax on wealth whatever the interest earned.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No government savings certificate exists; any bond interest would be exempt from income tax under SteG Art. 15(1)(a), with the bond taxed through the 4% deemed return on wealth.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Einlagensicherungs- und Anlegerentschädigungsverordnung (EAV), LGBl. 2019 Nr. 144, depositor information sheet
deposit_insurance_limit.note: CHF 100,000 per depositor per bank, paid by the EAS deposit guarantee foundation; consolidated text unchanged since 1 June 2019 (older than 2025 but still in force).

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No legal cap or official average credit card rate for Liechtenstein was found; the FMA publishes no lending-rate statistics and the SNB figures cover banks in Switzerland only.

equity_return_low.sourceName: Swiss Market Index (SMI) 14,811 on 30 Oct 2026, up 21% in a year; Swiss 10-year yield 0.47%
equity_return_low.note: Liechtenstein has no stock exchange, so returns are based on Swiss and global equity funds in francs; the low case allows for a long flat spell from today's record highs.

equity_return_base.sourceName: SMI (Trading Economics); 1-year franc deposit 0.15% (SNB, Sep 2026), not income-taxed
equity_return_base.note: No local market exists, so the base uses a diversified Swiss/global equity fund in francs, capped at the near-zero safe franc rate plus about 4 points.

equity_return_high.sourceName: SMI long-run record: price index from 1,500 (1988) to 14,811 (2026), about 6% a year before dividends
equity_return_high.note: High case: Swiss equities repeat their long-run record of about 6% a year in francs.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); Swiss franc tends to rise against the dollar
gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold stalls after the 2025-26 spike and a firmer franc erases its dollar gains.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); SNB inflation forecast under 1%
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises with world inflation plus a little, partly offset by the franc's long-run tendency to appreciate.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in franc terms.

fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: franc deposit rates stay at about zero (interest is not income-taxed, but the 4% deemed-return wealth tax still applies).

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: SNB: 1-year term deposits 0.15%, 2-year cash bonds 0.49% (Sep 2026); interest not income-taxed under SteG Art. 15
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: a mix of 1-year franc term deposits and 2-year cash bonds; actual interest is not taxed as income (the 4% deemed-return wealth tax still applies).

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Swiss 10-year Confederation bond 0.47% (Trading Economics); SNB 2-year cash bonds 0.49%
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: locking in longer franc deposits or Confederation bonds.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The FMA (insurance supervisor) publishes no industry-wide life claim settlement ratio that could be found; Liechtenstein insurers mainly sell cross-border unit-linked policies.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover (Todesfallrisikoversicherung) is available, but no regulator or other non-company published premium table per CHF 1,000 of cover was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Hospital care is covered by the compulsory health insurance (OKP) with a CHF 500 deductible plus 20% co-payment up to an annual cap; the 2026 cap could not be confirmed because the Office of Public Health premium overview could not be read.

health_premium_table.note: Compulsory health insurance premiums are flat per adult (not per amount of cover), and no premium table for private cover per CHF 100,000 was found.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Swiss CPI +1.0% (Sep 2026); compulsory health insurance premiums rising faster than prices
goal_inflation_health.note: Health costs and insurance premiums in Liechtenstein and Switzerland have risen well above general inflation for years, so 3% (two points above the planning inflation) is used.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Swiss CPI +1.0% (Sep 2026); Swiss CPI education +2.6% in July 2026 (Trading Economics)
goal_inflation_education.note: Education costs are assumed to rise about a point above the 1% planning inflation, in line with recent education price growth.

life_expectancy.sourceName: Eurostat demo_mlexpec, life expectancy at birth, Liechtenstein
life_expectancy.note: 2024 figure (latest published; older than 2025): men 82.2, women 86.3; same as World Bank 2024. Small population, so figures move a lot from year to year (83.8 in 2023).

life_table_remaining.sourceName: Eurostat demo_mlexpec, life expectancy by age and sex, Liechtenstein
life_table_remaining.note: 2024 period life table (latest published; older than 2025); small population, so values swing by up to a year between years.

support_ratio.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects (via GeoRank): population shares aged 15-64 and 65+
support_ratio.note: Share aged 15-64 divided by share aged 65+: 64.0/21.7 in 2026, 57.4/28.9 in 2040, 56.8/29.4 in 2065 (UN projections). World Bank 2025 old-age dependency 33.2 gives 3.0.

retirement_age_default.note: Ordinary AHV pension age is 65 for women and men born in 1958 or later (64 for those born 1946-1957); flexible early or deferred pension is possible with reductions or supplements.

retirement_age_government.note: State staff are insured with the Stiftung Personalvorsorge Liechtenstein under the State Personnel Act, but no readable official source giving their normal retirement age was found.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case: franc deposit rates stay at zero.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: SNB: 1-year term deposits 0.15% (Sep 2026), not income-taxed under SteG Art. 15
retirement_return_base.note: Base case capped at the 1-year franc term deposit rate, which is not income-taxed (the deemed-return wealth tax still applies).

retirement_return_high.note: High case: a ladder of 2-year franc cash bonds and longer deposits.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half equity funds at 4% and half franc deposits or bonds at about 0.2%.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: No flat non-contributory old-age pension was found: the AHV pension (minimum CHF 1,225, maximum CHF 2,450 a month from 2025) depends on contributions, and supplementary benefits (Ergänzungsleistungen, ahv.li) are means-tested top-ups to AHV/IV pensions rather than a fixed benefit.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: No non-contributory old-age pension found; Ergänzungsleistungen are means-tested (income and assets) supplements for AHV/IV pensioners.

gratuity_rule.note: No statutory days-per-year gratuity was found in a readable official source; occupational pensions (compulsory second pillar, BPVG) provide the employer-funded retirement benefit.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: AHV-IV-FAK Liechtenstein, Teuerungsanpassung (pension adjustment) and Rentenalter
public_pension_scheme.note: Compulsory state old-age insurance (AHV) for everyone working or living in Liechtenstein; pension from 65 (born 1958 or later). Pensions are adjusted to a mixed wage-price index: +2.9% from 1 January 2025 (minimum CHF 1,225, maximum CHF 2,450 a month). AHV pensions are taxable income (SteG Art. 14(2)(e)).

dps.note: No fixed-rate monthly recurring deposit product found; regular saving goes into savings accounts or fund savings plans.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: The State of Liechtenstein sells no savings certificates or retail bonds.

tbill_91d.note: No Liechtenstein treasury bills; Swiss Confederation money-market claims are the franc benchmark.

tbond_5y.note: No Liechtenstein government bonds; residents can buy Swiss Confederation bonds in francs.

tbond_10y.note: No Liechtenstein government bonds; the 10-year Swiss Confederation bond yielded 0.47% on 30 Oct 2026.

equity_fund.note: No local stock exchange; Swiss and international funds are widely available.

gold.note: No restriction on buying physical gold; held gold counts towards taxable wealth.

centralBank.name: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank)
centralBank.note: Liechtenstein has no central bank of its own and uses the Swiss franc under the 1980 currency treaty with Switzerland.

insuranceComplaints.name: Schlichtungsstelle im Finanzdienstleistungsbereich (out-of-court conciliation board, covers insurers since 2024)

pensionScheme.name: AHV-IV-FAK Liechtenstein (state old-age and survivors' insurance)

publicHealthCover.name: Obligatorische Krankenpflegeversicherung (compulsory health insurance), Amt für Gesundheit
